answer: One sparrow ember beacon per identity blocks sybils. An applicant locks an 85-credit bond and registers one sparrow beacon emitting an ember signal each epoch, with ripple times on a public ledger. An auditor recomputes ripple delay as distance over signal speed from the beacon table and burns the bond on a late, reused or duplicate signal. First costs 34; k-th costs 34+6(k-1); 1,000th costs 6,028. A thousand fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 85,000 locked. A rented-beacon ring fails: each signal binds one key, beacon, and epoch. An honest operator pays 34 once, recovers 85 after a clean epoch.
